answer: Tiered Throughput Decay. Each agent identity gets a base action rate, but the rate for identity N scales as 1/N^0.7 against the operator's verified billing inlet, so mass registration yields steeply diminishing capacity per identity. An attacker's cost per usable identity rises with fleet size, and the lotus of usable throughput stays capped. Operators pay escalating infrastructure and latency overhead; a velvet margin of real utility only survives at small N.
